source.title: Stress signalling pathways that impair prefrontal cortex structure and function

confidence_rationale: Canonical review establishing that even mild acute uncontrollable stress triggers a catecholamine surge that rapidly takes prefrontal deliberative control offline and shifts behaviour toward habitual/reactive responding. This is the neuromodulatory mechanism behind anti-epistemic-panic: under threat the substrate that would sustain extended inference is suppressed, forcing early commitment. Strong source; capped because it is about working-memory/PFC function generally, and the bridge to REE's specific commitment-timing gate is functional, not implemented.
failure_signatures: Anti-epistemic-panic mechanism: acute stress -> high catecholamines -> PFC deliberative/working-memory function impaired -> reliance on faster habitual/subcortical control -> commitment before the belief-state is resolved.
Predicts the inverted-U: too little arousal under-engages, too much collapses deliberation -- the commitment-timing axis has an optimal band, not a monotone.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Acute uncontrollable stress engages catecholamine (noradrenaline/dopamine) signalling that, at high levels, rapidly and reversibly impairs prefrontal cortex function and shifts behavioural control from slow, flexible PFC-mediated deliberation toward faster, habitual posterior/subcortical circuits.
mapping.ree_translation: Supplies the neuromodulatory why for the anti-epistemic-panic pole of MECH-434: under threat-driven arousal the capacity for extended, flexible inference is down-regulated, biasing the commitment-timing parameter toward premature commitment. It also grounds MECH-434's inverted-U structure (an optimal arousal band) and links the axis to a future REE neuromodulatory analogue (cf. the LC-NE-analog gap noted across the V4 sweep).
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review concerns biological PFC working memory under catecholamine stress; REE has no literal catecholamine system and the link to its commitment gate (MECH-090) is functional analogy. It grounds that arousal CAN collapse deliberation, not that REE's substrate does so by this pathway.
mapping.source_context: Mechanistic neuroscience review (rodent + primate + human) of acute/chronic stress effects on prefrontal cortex via catecholamine intracellular signalling.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical Nat Rev Neurosci review. Mapping fidelity moderate (general PFC function -> REE commitment gate is analogy); transfer risk moderate (no catecholamine substrate in REE).
